claims.text: The multilayer coatings consist of alternating nanoscale layers that differ in composition.
A homogeneous comparator can have the same overall composition as the multilayer coating while lacking its engineered interfaces.
Chemically dissimilar nanoscale interfaces impede dislocation glide.
Chemically dissimilar nanoscale interfaces impede dislocation climb.
The multilayer interfaces retard atomic diffusion across the interfaces.
Retarding interfacial diffusion slows diffusion-controlled deformation processes.
Blocking dislocation motion and retarding diffusion reduce time-dependent plastic deformation relative to a homogeneous structure.
Elevated temperature and constant applied stress can activate creep in these materials.
The multilayer coating will exhibit statistically significantly lower creep strain than the homogeneous comparator under identical temperature and stress conditions.
The multilayer coating may show delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to the homogeneous comparator.
The proposed effect applies when temperature is high enough to activate creep but low enough to preserve the multilayer interfaces.
The proposed effect applies when layer thickness is comparable to or smaller than characteristic dislocation-loop sizes.
The magnitude of creep reduction may depend on the alloy system and layer thickness.
A controlled comparison should use multilayer and homogeneous samples with identical overall composition under identical creep-test conditions.
Failure to observe either lower creep strain rates or delayed plastic deformation in the multilayer sample would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes the homogeneous comparator as a bulk alloy, whereas the baseline and experimental design describe it as a coating. Bulk and coating comparators are not equivalent geometries and could introduce uncontrolled size, substrate, and processing differences.
